transcript.text: We had a power cut last night and now our Candy washer dryer is completely dead - no lights, nothing. Everything else in the house came back on. The plug fuse is fine, I swapped it. Help!

A power cut and surge can sometimes blow internal safety fuses or damage the main PCB even if the house supply is fine. Since the plug fuse is good but there are no lights at all, we need to narrow this down. Please find the model number on a sticker inside the door rim or on the back of the door so I can check the specific wiring and components for your Candy washer-dryer.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
The label says CSOW 4965TWE/1-80, it's a Candy Smart Pro. About 3 years old. No burning smell or anything from it, just totally dead.

Thanks for that model number. This is a common protective measure in modern electronics. Please unplug the machine completely. Remove the rear panel (usually four screws) to expose the internal wiring. Look for where the mains cable enters; there should be a small glass tube or ceramic block fuse mounted on the circuit board or near the socket. Check if the wire inside the glass is broken or if the ceramic element shows blackening/blow marks. If that internal fuse is blown, replacing it might fix it (though a surge can also damage the PCB). If the fuse is intact, the issue may be deeper in the electronics.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.

Sorry, I'm not going to take the back panel off or poke about with the internal electrics. I've already tried the socket (a lamp works in it), a new plug fuse, and leaving it unplugged for over 10 minutes. Still dead. Is there anything else I can check, or do I need an engineer?

As there are no lights at all, this is an electrical fault that cannot be fixed with simple owner checks. You will need to call an engineer to inspect and repair the internal electronics.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.
